0: In the beginning God created heaven, and earth.
1: And the earth was void and empty, and darkness was upon the face of the deep; and the spirit of God moved over the waters.
2: And God said: Be light made. And light was made.
3: And God saw the light that it was good; and he divided the light from the darkness.
4: And he called the light Day, and the darkness Night; and there was evening and morning one day.
5: And God said: Let there be a firmament made amidst the waters: and let it divide the waters from the waters.
6: And God made a firmament, and divided the waters that were under the firmament, from those that were above the firmament, and it was so.
7: And God called the firmament, Heaven; and the evening and morning were the second day.
8: God also said: Let the waters that are under the heaven, be gathered together into one place: and let the dry land appear. And it was so done.
9: And God called the dry land, Earth; and the gathering together of the waters, he called Seas. And God saw that it was good.
10: And he said: Let the earth bring forth the green herb, and such as may seed, and the fruit tree yielding fruit after its kind, which may have seed in itself upon the earth. And it was so done.
11: And the earth brought forth the green herb, and such as yieldeth seed according to its kind, and the tree that beareth fruit having seed each one according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.
12: And the evening and the morning were the third day.
13: And God said: Let there be lights made in the firmament of heaven, to divide the day and the night, and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days and years:
14: To shine in the firmament of heaven, and to give light upon the earth. And it was so done.
15: And God made two great lights: a greater light to rule the day; and a lesser light to rule the night: and the stars.
16: And he set them in the firmament of heaven to shine upon the earth.
18: And the evening and morning were the fourth day.
19: God also said: Let the waters bring forth the creeping creature having life, and the fowl that may fly over the earth under the firmament of heaven.
20: And God created the great whales, and every living and moving creature, which the waters brought forth, according to their kinds, and every winged fowl according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.
21: And he blessed them, saying: Increase and multiply, and fill the waters of the sea: and let the birds be multiplied upon the earth.
22: And the evening and morning were the fifth day.
23: And God said: Let the earth bring forth the living creature in its kind, cattle and creeping things, and beasts of the earth, according to their kinds. And it was so done.
24: And God made the beasts of the earth according to their kinds, and cattle, and every thing that creepeth on the earth after its kind. And God saw that it was good.
25: And he said: Let us make man to our image and likeness: and let him have dominion over the fishes of the sea, and the fowls of the air, and the beasts, and the whole earth, and every creeping creature that moveth upon the earth.
26: And God created man to his own image: to the image of God he created him: male and female he created them.
27: And God blessed them, saying: Increase and multiply, and fill the earth, and subdue it, and rule over the fishes of the sea, and the fowls of the air, and all living creatures that move upon the earth.
28: And God said: Behold I have given you every herb bearing seed upon the earth, and all trees that have in themselves seed of their own kind, to be your meat:
29: And to all the beasts of the earth, and to every fowl of the air, and to all that move upon the earth, and wherein there is life, that they may have to feed upon. And it was so done.
30: And God saw all the things that he had made, and they were very good. And the evening and morning were the sixth day.
31: So the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the furniture of them.
32: And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made: and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had done.
33: And he blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because in it he had rested from all his work which God created and made.
34: These are the generations of the heaven and the earth, when they were created, in the day that the Lord God made the heaven and the earth:
35: And every plant of the field before it spring up in the earth, and every herb of the ground before it grew: for the Lord God had not rained upon the earth; and there was not a man to till the earth.
36: But a spring rose out the earth, watering all the surface of the earth.
37: And the Lord God formed man of the slime of the earth: and breathed into his face the breath of life, and man became a living soul.
38: And the Lord God had planted a paradise of pleasure from the beginning: wherein he placed man whom he had formed.
39: And the Lord God brought forth of the ground all manner of trees, fair to behold, and pleasant to eat of: the tree of life also in the midst of paradise: and the tree of knowledge of good and evil.
40: And a river went out the place of pleasure to water paradise, which from thence is divided into four heads.
41: The name of the one is Phison: that is it which compasseth all the land of Hevilath, where gold groweth.
42: And the gold of that land is very good: there is found bdellium, and the onyx stone.
43: And the name of the second river is Gehon: the same is it that compasseth all the land of Ethiopia
44: And the name of the third river is Tigris: the same passeth along by the Assyrians. And the fourth river is Euphrates.
45: And the Lord God took man, and put him into the paradise for pleasure, to dress it, and keep it.
46: And he commanded him, saying: Of every tree of paradise thou shalt eat:
47: But of the tree of knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat. for in what day soever thou shalt eat of it, thou shalt die the death.
48: And the Lord God said: It is not good for man to be alone: let us make him a help like unto himself.
49: And the Lord God having formed out of the ground all the beasts of the earth, and all the fowls of the air, brought them to Adam to see what he would call them: for whatsoever Adam called any living creature the same is its name.
50: And Adam called all the beasts by their names, and all the fowls of the air, and all the cattle of the field: but for Adam there was not found a helper like himself.
51: Then the Lord God cast a deep sleep upon Adam: and when he was fast asleep, he took one of his ribs, and filled up flesh for it.
52: And the Lord God built the rib which he took from Adam into a woman: and brought her to Adam.
53: And Adam said: This now is bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called woman, because she was taken out of man.
54: Wherefore a man shall leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they shall be two in one flesh.
55: And they were both naked: to wit, Adam and his wife: and were not ashamed.
56: Now the serpent was more subtle than any of the beasts of the earth which the Lord God made. And he said to the woman: Why hath God commanded you, that you should not eat of every tree of paradise?
57: And the woman answered him, saying: Of the fruit of the trees that are in paradise we do eat:
58: But of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of paradise, God hath commanded us that we should not eat; and that we should not touch it, lest perhaps we die.
59: And the serpent said to the woman: No, you shall not die the death.
60: For God doth know that in what day soever you shall eat thereof, your eyes shall be opened: and you shall be as Gods, knowing good and evil.
61: And the woman saw that the tree was good to eat, and fair to the eyes, and delightful to behold: and she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave to her husband who did eat.
62: And the eyes of them both were opened: and when they perceived themselves to be naked, they sewed together fig leaves, and made themselves aprons.
63: And when they heard the voice of the Lord God walking in paradise at the afternoon air, Adam and his wife hid themselves from the face of the Lord God, amidst the trees of paradise.
64: And the Lord God called Adam, and said to him: Where art thou?
65: And he said: I heard thy voice in paradise; and I was afraid, because I was naked, and I hid myself.
66: And he said to him: And who hath told thee that thou wast naked, but that thou hast eaten of the tree whereof I commanded thee that thou shouldst not eat?
67: And Adam said: The woman, whom thou gavest me to be my companion, gave me of the tree, and I did eat.
68: And the Lord God said to the woman: Why hast thou done this? And she answered: The serpent deceived me, and I did eat.
69: And the Lord God said to the serpent: Because thou hast done this thing, thou art cursed among all cattle, and the beasts of the earth: upon thy breast shalt thou go, and earth shalt thou eat all the days of thy life.
70: I will put enmities between thee and the woman, and thy seed and her seed: she shall crush thy head, and thou shalt lie in wait for her heel.
71: To the woman also he said: I will multiply thy sorrows, and thy conceptions: in sorrow shalt thou bring forth children, and thou shalt be under thy husband’s power, and he shall have dominion over thee.
72: And to Adam he said: Because thou hast hearkened to the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, whereof I commanded thee that thou shouldst not eat, cursed is the earth in thy work; with labour and toil shalt thou eat thereof all the days of thy life.
73: Thorns and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou eat the herbs of the earth.
74: In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread till thou return to the earth, out of which thou wast taken: for dust thou art, and into dust thou shalt return.
75: And Adam called the name of his wife Eve: because she was the mother of all the living.
76: And the Lord God made for Adam and his wife, garments of skins, and clothed them.
77: And he said: Behold Adam is become as one of us, knowing good and evil: now, therefore, lest perhaps he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever.
78: And the Lord God sent him out of the paradise of pleasure, to till the earth from which he was taken.
79: And he cast out Adam; and placed before the paradise of pleasure Cherubims, and a flaming sword, turning every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.
80: And Adam knew Eve his wife: who conceived and brought forth Cain, saying: I have gotten a man through God.
81: And again she brought forth his brother Abel. And Abel was a shepherd, and Cain a husbandman.
82: And it came to pass after many days, that Cain offered, of the fruits of the earth, gifts to the Lord.
83: Abel also offered of the firstlings of his flock, and of their fat: and the Lord had respect to Abel, and to his offerings.
84: But to Cain and his offerings he had no respect: and Cain was exceedingly angry, and his countenance fell.
85: And the Lord said to him: Why art thou angry? and why is thy countenance fallen?
86: If thou do well, shalt thou not receive? but if ill, shall not sin forthwith be present at the door? but the lust thereof shall be under thee, and thou shalt have dominion over it.
87: And Cain said to Abel his brother: Let us go forth abroad. And when they were in the field, Cain rose up against his brother Abel, and slew him.
88: And the Lord said to Cain: Where is thy brother Abel? And he answered, I know not: am I my brother’s keeper?
89: And he said to him: What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother’s blood crieth to me from the earth.
90: Now, therefore, cursed shalt thou be upon the earth, which hath opened her mouth and received the blood of thy brother at thy hand,
91: When thou shalt till it, it shall not yield to thee its fruit: a fugitive and vagabond shalt thou be upon the earth.
92: And Cain said to the Lord: My iniquity is greater than that I may deserve pardon.
93: Behold thou dost cast me out this day from the face of the earth, and I shall be hidden from thy face, and I shall be a vagabond and a fugitive on the earth: everyone, therefore, that findeth me, shall kill me.
94: And the Lord said to him: No, it shall not be so: but whosoever shall kill Cain, shall be punished sevenfold. And the Lord set a mark upon Cain, that whosoever found him should not kill him.
95: And Cain went out from the face of the Lord, and dwelt as a fugitive on the earth, at the east side of Eden.
96: And Cain knew his wife, and she conceived, and brought forth Henoch: and he built a city, and called the name thereof by the name of his son Henoch.
97: And Henoch begot Irad, and Irad begot Maviael, and Maviael begot Mathusael, and Mathusael begot Lamech:
98: Who took two wives: the name of the one was Ada, and the name of the other was Sella.
99: And Ada brought forth Jabel: who was the father of such as dwell in tents, and of herdsmen.
100: And his brother’s name was Jubal; he was the father of them that play upon the harp and the organs.
101: Sella also brought forth Tubalcain, who was a hammerer and artificer in every work of brass and iron. And the sister of Tubalcain was Noema.
102: And Lamech said to his wives Ada and Sell: Hear my voice, ye wives of Lamech, hearken to my speech: for I have slain a man to the wounding of myself, and a stripling to my own bruising.
103: Sevenfold vengeance shall be taken for Cain: but for Lamech seventy times sevenfold.
104: Adam also knew his wife again: and she brought forth a son, and called his name Seth, saying: God hath given me another seed, for Abel whom Cain slew.
105: But to Seth also was born a son, whom he called Enos; this man began to call upon the name of the Lord.
106: This is the book of the generation of Adam. In the day that God created man, he made him to the likeness of God.
108: And Adam lived a hundred and thirty years, and begot a son to his own image and likeness, and called his name Seth.
109: And the days of Adam, after he begot Seth, were eight hundred years: and he begot sons and daughters.
110: And all the time that Adam lived came to nine hundred and thirty years, and he died.
111: Seth also lived a hundred and five years, and begot Enos.
112: And Seth lived after he begot Enos, eight hundred and seven years, and begot sons and daughters.
113: And all the days of Seth were nine hundred and twelve years, and he died.
114: And Enos lived ninety years, and begot Cainan.
115: After whose birth he lived eight hundred and fifteen years, and begot sons and daughters.
117: And Cainan lived seventy years, and begot Malaleel.
118: And Cainan lived after he begot Malaleel, eight hundred forty years, and begot sons and daughters.
119: And all the days of Cainan were nine hundred and ten years, and he died.
120: And Malaleel lived sixty-five years, and begot Jared.
126: And Henoch lived sixty-five years, and begot Mathusala.
127: And Henoch walked with God: and lived after he begot Mathusala, three hundred years, and begot sons and daughters.
129: And he walked with God, and was seen no more: because God took him.
130: And Mathusala lived a hundred and eighty-seven years, and begot Lamech.
134: And he called his name Noe, saying: This same shall comfort us from the works and labours of our hands on the earth which the Lord hath cursed.
137: And Noe, when he was five hundred years old, begot Sem, Cham, and Japheth.
138: And after that men began to be multiplied upon the earth, and daughters were born to them.
139: The sons of God seeing the daughters of men, that they were fair, took themselves wives of all which they chose.
140: And God said: My spirit shall not remain in man for ever, because he is flesh, and his days shall be a hundred and twenty years.
141: Now giants were upon the earth in those days. For after the sons of God went in to the daughters of men and they brought forth children, these are the mighty men of old, men of renown.
142: And God seeing that the wickedness of men was great on the earth, and that all the thought of their heart was bent upon evil at all times,
143: It repented him that he had made man on the earth. And being touched inwardly with sorrow of heart,
144: He said: I will destroy man, whom I have created, from the face of the earth, from man even to beasts, from the creeping thing even to the fowls of the air, for it repenteth me that I have made them.
145: But Noe found grace before the Lord.
146: These are the generations of Noe: Noe was a just and perfect man in his generations, he walked with God.
148: And the earth was corrupted before God, and was filled with iniquity.
150: He said to Noe: The end of all flesh is come before me, the earth is filled with iniquity through them, and I will destroy them with the earth.
151: Make thee an ark of timber planks: thou shalt make little rooms in the ark, and thou shalt pitch it within and without.
152: And thus shalt thou make it: The length of the ark shall be three hundred cubits: the breadth of it fifty cubits, and the height of it thirty cubits.
153: Thou shalt make a window in the ark, and in a cubit shalt thou finish the top of it: and the door of the ark thou shalt set in the side: with lower, middle chambers, and third stories shalt thou make it.
154: Behold I will bring the waters of a great flood upon the earth, to destroy all flesh, wherein is the breath of life, under heaven. All things that are in the earth shall be consumed.
155: And I will establish my covenant with thee, and thou shalt enter into the ark, thou and thy sons, and thy wife, and the wives of thy sons with thee.
156: And of every living creature of all flesh, thou shalt bring two of each sort into the ark, that they may live with thee: of the male sex, and the female.
158: Thou shalt take unto thee of all food that may be eaten, and thou shalt lay it up with thee: and it shall be food for thee and them.
160: And the Lord said to him: Go in thou and all thy house into the ark: for thee I have seen just before me in this generation.
161: Of all clean beasts take seven and seven, the male and female.
162: But of the beasts that are unclean two and two, the male and female. Of the fowls also of the air seven and seven,the male and the female: that seed may be saved upon the face of the whole earth.
163: For yet a while, and after seven days, I will rain upon the earth forty days and forty nights; and I will destroy every substance that I have made, from the face of the earth.
165: And he was six hundred years old, when the waters of the flood overflowed the earth.
169: And after seven days were passed, the waters of the flood overflowed the earth.
170: In the six hundreth year of the life of Noe in the second month, in the seventeenth day of the month, all the fountains of the great deep were broken up, and the flood gates of heaven were open:
172: In the selfsame day Noe, and Sem, and Cham, and Japheth his sons: his wife, and the three wives of his sons with them, went into the ark:
173: They and every beast according to its kind, and all the cattle in their kind, and every thing that moveth upon the earth according to its kind, and every fowl according to its kind, and every fowl according to its kind, all birds, and all that fly.
175: And they that went in, went in male and female of all flesh, as God had commanded him: and the Lord shut him in on the outside.
176: And the flood was forty days upon the earth, and the waters increased, and lifted up the ark on high from earth.
177: For they overflowed exceedingly: and filled all on the face of the earth: and the ark was carried upon the waters.
178: And the waters prevailed beyond measure upon the earth: and all the high mountains under the whole heaven were covered.
179: The water was fifteen cubits higher than the mountains which it covered.
180: And all flesh was destroyed that moved upon the earth, both of fowl, and of cattle, and of beasts, and of all creeping things that creep upon the earth: and all men.
182: And he destroyed all the substance that was upon the earth, from man to beast, and the creeping things and fowls of the air: and they were destroyed from the earth: and Noe only remained, and they that were with him in the ark.
184: And God remembered Noe, and all the living creatures, and all the cattle which were with him in the ark, and brought a wind upon the earth, and the waters were abated.
185: The fountains also of the deep, and the flood gates of heaven were shut up, and the rain from heaven was restrained.
186: And the waters returned from off the earth going and coming: and they began to be abated after a hundred and fifty days.
187: And the ark rested in the seventh month, the seven and twentieth day of the month, upon the mountains of Armenia.
188: And the waters were going and decreasing until the tenth month: for in the tenth month, the first day of the month, the tops of the mountains appeared.
189: And after that forty days were passed, Noe, opening the window of the ark which he had made, sent forth a raven:
190: Which went forth and did not return, till the waters were dried up upon the earth.
191: He sent forth also a dove after him, to see if the waters had now ceased upon the face of the earth.
192: But she, not finding where her foot might rest, returned to him into the ark: for the waters were upon the whole earth: and he put forth his hand, and caught her, and brought her into the ark.
193: And having waited yet seven other days, he again sent forth the dove out of the ark.
194: And she came to him in the evening, carrying a bough of an olive tree, with green leaves, in her mouth. Noe therefore understood that the waters were ceased upon the earth.
195: And he stayed yet other seven days: and he sent forth the dove, which returned not any more unto him.
196: Therefore in the six hundreth and first year, the first month, the first day of the month, the waters were lessened upon the earth, and Noe opening the covering of the ark, looked, and saw that the face of the earth was dried.
198: And God spoke to Noe, saying:
200: All livings things that are with thee of all flesh, as well in fowls as in beasts, and all creeping things that creep upon the earth, bring out with thee, and go ye upon the earth: increased and multiply upon it.
203: And Noe built an altar unto the Lord: and taking of all cattle and fowls that were clean, offered holocausts upon the altar.
204: And the Lord smelled a sweet savour, and said: I will no more curse the earth for the sake of man: for the imagination and thought of man’s heart are prone to evil from his youth: therefore I will no more destroy every living soul as I have done.
205: All the days of the earth, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, night and day, shall not cease.
207: And let the fear and dread of you be upon all the beasts of the earth, and upon all the fowls of the air, and all that move upon the earth: all the fishes of the sea are delivered into your hand.
208: And every thing that moveth and liveth shall be meat for you: even as the green herbs have I delivered them all to you:
209: Saving that flesh with blood you shall not eat.
210: For I will require the blood of your lives at the hand of every beast, and at the hand of man, at the hand of every man, and of his brother, will I require the life of man.
211: Whosoever shall shed man’s blood, his blood shall be shed: for man was made to the image of God.
216: I will establish my covenant with you, and all flesh shall be no more destroyed with the waters of a flood, neither shall there be from henceforth a flood to waste the earth.
217: And God said: This is the sign of the covenant which I will give between me and you, and to every living soul that is with you, for perpetual generations.
218: I will set my bow in the clouds, and it shall be the sign of a covenant between me, and between the earth.
219: And when I shall cover the sky with clouds, my bow shall appear in the clouds:
220: And I will remember my covenant with you, and with every living soul that beareth flesh: and there shall no more be waters of a flood to destroy all flesh.
221: And the bow shall be in the clouds, and I shall see it, and shall remember the everlasting covenant, that was made between God and every living soul of all flesh which is upon the earth.
222: And God said to Noe: This shall be the sign of the covenant which I have established between me and all flesh upon the earth.
223: And the sons of Noe who came out of the ark, were Sem, Cham, and Japheth: and Cham is the father of Chanaan.
224: These three are the sons of Noe: and from these was all mankind spread over the whole earth.
225: And Noe, a husbandman, began to till the ground, and planted a vineyard.
226: And drinking of the wine was made drunk, and was uncovered in his tent.
227: Which when Cham the father of Chaanan had seen, to wit, that his father’s nakedness was uncovered, he told it to his two brethren without.
228: But Sem and Japheth put a cloak upon their shoulders, and going backward, covered the nakedness of their father: and their faces were turned away, and they saw not their father’s nakedness.
229: And Noe awaking from the wine, when he had learned what his younger son had done to him,
230: He said: Cursed be Chaanan, a servant of servants, shall he be unto his brethren.
232: May God enlarge Japheth, and may he dwell in the tents of Sem, and Chanaan be his servant.
236: The sons of Japheth: Gomer, and Magog, and Madai, and Javan, and Thubal, and Mosoch, and Thiras.
237: And the sons of Gomer: Ascenez and Riphath and Thogorma.
238: And the sons of Javan: Elisa and Tharsis, Cetthim, and Dodanim.
239: By these were divided the islands of the Gentiles in their lands, every one according to his tongue and their families in their nations.
240: And the sons of Cham: Chus, and Mesram, and Phuth, and Chanaan.
241: And the sons of Chus: Saba and Hevila, and Sabatha, and Regma, and Sabatacha. The sons of Regma: Saba and Dadan.
242: Now Chus begot Nemrod: he began to be mighty on earth.
243: And he was a stout hunter before the Lord. Hence came a proverb: Even as Nemrod the stout hunter before the Lord.
244: And the beginning of his kingdom was Babylon, and Arach, and Achad, and Chalanne in the land of Sennaar.
245: Out of that land came forth Assur, and built Ninive, and the streets of the city, and Chale.
246: Resen also between Ninive and Chale: this is the great city.
247: And Mesraim begot Ludim, and Anamim, and Laabim, Nepthuim,
248: And Phetrusim, and Chasluim; of whom came forth the Philistines, and the Capthorim.
249: And Chanaan begot Sidon, his firstborn, the Hethite,
250: And the Jebusite, and the Amorrhite, and the Gergesite,
251: The Hevite and the Aracite: the Sinite,
252: And the Aradian, the Samarite, and the Hamathite: and afterwards the families of the Chanaanites were spread abroad.
253: And the limits of Chanaan were from Sidon as one comes to Gerara even to Gaza, until thou enter Sodom and Gomorrha, and Adama, and Seboim even to Lesa.
254: These are the children of Cham in their kindreds, and tongues, and generations, and lands, and nations.
255: Of Sem also, the father of all children of Heber, the elder brother of Japheth, sons were born.
256: The sons of Sem: Elam and Assur, and Arphaxad, and Lud, and Aram.
257: The sons of Aram: Us and Hull, and Gether: and Mess.
258: But Arphaxad begot Sale, of whom was born Heber.
259: And to Heber were born two sons: the name of the one was Phaleg, because in his days the earth was divided: and his brother’s name Jectan.
260: Which Jectan begot Elmodad, and Saleph, and Asarmoth, Jare,
261: And Anduram, and Uzal, and Decla,
263: And Ophir, and Hevila, and Jobab.
264: And their dwelling was from Messa as we go on as far as Sephar, a mountain in the east.
265: These are the children of Sem according to their kindreds and tongues, and countries in their nations.
266: These are the families of Noe, according to their peoples and nations. By these were the nations divided on the earth after the flood.
268: And when they removed from the east, they found a plain in the land of Sennaar, and dwelt in it.
269: And each one said to his neighbour: Come, let us make brick, and bake them of stones, and slime instead of mortar.
270: And they said: Come, let us make a city and a tower, the top whereof may reach to heaven: and let us make our name famous before we be scattered abroad into all lands.
271: And the Lord came down to see the city and the tower, which the children of Adam were building.
272: And he said: Behold, it is one people, and all have one tongue: and they have begun to do this, neither will they leave off from their designs, till they accomplish them in deed.
273: Come ye, therefore, let us go down, and there may not understand one another’s speech.
274: And so the Lord scattered them from that place into all lands, and they ceased to build the city.
275: And therefore the name thereof was called Babel, because there the language of the whole earth was confounded: and from thence the Lord scattered them abroad upon the face of all countries.
284: Phaleg also lived thirty years, and begot Reu.
286: And Reu lived thirty-two years, and begot Sarug.
288: And Sarug lived thirty years, and begot Nachor.
290: And Nachor lived nine and twenty years, and begot Thare.
291: And Nachor lived after he begot Thare, a hundred and nineteen years: and begot sons and daughters.
292: And Thare lived seventy years, and begot Abram, and Nachor, and Aran.
293: And these are the generations of Thare: Thare begot Abram, Nachor, and Aran. And Aran begot Lot.
294: And Aran died before Thare his father, in the land of his nativity in Ur of the Chaldees.
295: And Abram and Nachor married wives: the name of Abram’s wife was Sarai: and the name of Nachor’s wife, Melcha, the daughter of Aran, father of Melcha, and father of Jescha.

1939: For Pharao went in on horseback with his chariots and horsemen into the sea: and the Lord brought back upon them the waters of the sea: but the children of Israel walked on dry ground in the midst thereof.
1940: So Mary the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a timbrel in her hand: and all the women went forth after her with timbrels and with dances:
1941: And she began the song to them, saying: Let us sing to the Lord, for he is gloriously magnified, the horse and his rider he hath thrown into the sea.
1943: And they came into Mara, and they could not drink the waters of Mara, because they were bitter: whereupon he gave a name also agreeable to the place, calling it Mara, that is, bitterness.
1944: And the people murmured against Moses, saying: What shall we drink?
1945: But he cried to the Lord, and he shewed him a tree, which when he had cast into the waters, they were turned into sweetness. There he appointed him ordinances, and judgments, and there he proved him,
1946: Saying: If thou wilt hear the voice of the Lord thy God, and do what is right before him, and obey his commandments, and keep all his precepts, none of the evils that I laid upon Egypt, will I bring upon thee: for I am the Lord thy healer.
1947: And the children of Israel came into Elim, where there were twelve fountains of water, and seventy palm trees: and they encamped by the waters.
1948: And they set forward from Elim, and all the multitude of the children of Israel came into the desert of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai: the fifteenth day of the second month, after they came out of the land of Egypt.
1949: And all the congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness.
1950: And the children of Israel said to them: Would to God we had died by the hand of the Lord in the land of Egypt, when we sat over the flesh pots, and ate bread to the full. Why have you brought us into this desert, that you might destroy all the multitude with famine?
1951: And the Lord said to Moses: Behold I will rain bread from heaven for you: let the people go forth, and gather what is sufficient for every day: that I may prove them whether they will walk in my law, or not.
1954: And in the morning you shall see the glory of the Lord: for he hath heard your murmuring against the Lord: but as for us, what are we, that you mutter against us?
1955: And Moses said: In the evening the Lord will give you flesh to eat, and in the morning bread to the full: for he hath heard your murmurings, with which you have murmured against him, for what are we? your murmuring is not against us, but against the Lord.
1960: So it came to pass in the evening, that quails coming up, covered the camp: and in the morning, a dew lay round about the camp.
1961: And when it had covered the face of the earth, it appeared in the wilderness small, and as it were beaten with a pestle, like unto the hoar frost on the ground.
1962: And when the children of Israel saw it, they said one to another: Manhu! which signifieth: What is this! for they knew not what it was. And Moses said to them: This is the bread, which the Lord hath given you to eat.
1963: This is the word, that the Lord hath commanded: Let every one gather of it as much as is enough to eat: a gomor for every man, according to the number of your souls that dwell in a tent, so shall you take of it.
1965: And they measured by the measure of a gomor: neither had he more that had gathered more: nor did he find less that had provided less: but every one had gathered, according to what they were able to eat.
1967: And they hearkened not to him, but some of them left until the morning, and it began to be full of worms, an it putrefied, and Moses was angry with them.
1968: Now every one of them gathered in the morning, as much as might suffice to eat: and after the sun grew hot, it melted.
1969: But on the sixth day they gathered twice as much, that is, two gomors every man: and all the rulers of the multitude came, and told Moses.
1970: And he said to them: This is what the Lord hath spoken: To morrow is the rest of the sabbath sanctified to the Lord. Whatsoever work is to be done, do it: and the meats that are to be dressed, dress them: and whatsoever shall remain, lay it up until the morning.
1971: And they did so as Moses had commanded, and it did not putrefy, neither was there worm found in it.
1978: And the house of Israel called the name thereof Manna: and it was like coriander seed white, and the taste thereof like to flour with honey.
1980: And Moses said to Aaron: Take a vessel, and put manna into it, as much as a gomor can hold: and lay it up before the Lord to keep unto your generations,
1981: As the Lord commanded Moses. And Aaron put it in the tabernacle to be kept.
1982: And the children of Israel ate manna forty years, till they came to a habitable land: with this meat were they fed, until they reached the borders of the land of Chanaan.
1983: Now a gomor is the tenth part of an ephi.
1984: Then all the multitude of the children of Israel setting forward from the desert of Sin, by their mansions, according to the word of the Lord, encamped in Raphidim, where there was no water for the people to drink.
1985: And they chode with Moses, and said: Give us water, that we may drink. And Moses answered them: Why chide you with me? Wherefore do you tempt the Lord?
1986: So the people were thirsty there for want of water, and murmured against Moses, saying: Why didst thou make us go forth out of Egypt, to kill us and our children, and our beasts with thirst?
1989: Behold I will stand there before thee, upon the rock Horeb: and thou shalt strike the rock, and water shall come out of it that the people may drink. Moses did so before the ancients of Israel:
1990: And he called the name of that place Temptation, because the chiding of the children of Israel, and for that they tempted the Lord, saying: Is the Lord amongst us or not?
1991: And Amalec came, and fought against Israel in Raphidim.
1992: And Moses said to Josue: Choose out men: and go out and fight against Amalec: to morrow I will stand on the top of the hill having the rod of God in my hand.
1993: Josue did as Moses had spoken, and he fought against Amalec; but Moses, and Aaron, and Hur went up upon the top of the hill.
1994: And when Moses lifted up his hands, Israel overcame: but if he let them down a little, Amalec overcame.
1995: And Moses’ hands were heavy: so they took a stone, and put under him, and he sat on it: and Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands on both sides. And it came to pass that his hands were not weary until sunset.
1996: And Josue put Amalec and his people to flight, by the edge of the sword.
1997: And the Lord said to Moses: Write this for a memorial in a book, and deliver it to the ears of Josue: for I will destroy the memory of Amalec from under heaven.
1998: And Moses built an altar: and called the name thereof, The Lord my exaltation, saying:
